title: Signal Clinic: Discordant Asks and Micro-Patches
content:
Quick summary: This is a stitch-together note from the week of customer calls (9/6–9/10) + triage with eng. Goal: capture smaller, high-confidence fixes and surface 2 exploratory plays for product. Tone = scrappy; treat as working backlog for the next two sprints.

Observed patterns (high level):
- Discordant asks: same underlying problem but customers phrase it as separate feature requests (routing fails, model fallbacks, cost spikes). We should map to common causes not to feature names.
- Surface-level pain: inability to pin fallback model per route; teams resort to brittle client-side logic.
- Observability blind spots: token-level cost attribution looks good but teams lack per-prompt tracebacks to tie user complaint -> model decision (which model, why fallback).
- Usability: console rollout UI frequently confuses product teams when canary % + multiple rollouts exist; customers hit wrong variant.

Raw asks (verbatim examples):
- "We want to force the LLM to use the smaller model if latency > 500ms" (acct Alpha)
- "Give us a simple toggle to always prefer cheaper variants for embeddings" (acct Beta)
- "When the fallback happens, show me the full route and reason in the audit log" (acct Gamma)

Approx frequency / impact (quick heuristics):
- Routing pin/fallback control: reported by ~6 strategic customers this quarter; impact = high (production incidents).
- Rollout confusion in console: ~12 support tickets since July; impact = medium-high (incorrect experiments).
- Traceability for per-prompt routing decisions: ~8 asks; impact = high for regulated customers.

Micro-patch ideas (candidate quick wins, 1–2 sprint engineering scope):
1) "Fallback reason” field in audit logs + alert label. Add one-line reason codes (e.g., CAPACITY_FALLBACK, LATENCY_POLICY). UI exposes filter. Acceptance criteria: support ticket reproducer shows reason, customers can filter audit log by reason. Owner: eng-observability + CS. Risk: minor schema migration.
2) Console rollout preview: when you create a canary, show deterministic mapping of a sample request to variant (based on user_id hash + rollout rules). Acceptance: non-engineer tester can reproduce which variant a given user_id will hit. Owner: product-console. Risk: UX edge cases with multiple rules.
3) Cheap-variant toggle for embeddings: per-route checkbox + server-side preference flag (non-blocking). Acceptance: create route with toggle, embedding calls prefer cheaper model unless explicit override. Owner: product-hosted-api. Risk: quality regressions; need telemetry.

Exploratory plays (longer, cross-team):
- "Routing policy sandbox": an in-console simulator where customers upload 50 sample requests and simulate routing under different policies (latency-first, cost-first, reserved-capacity-first). Outcome: reduce misconfiguration and support load. Est. 4–6 sprints.
- "Transparent fallback contracts": define a short SLA doc + machine-readable fallback contract (what clients can expect when fallback happens). Helps enterprise legal + SRE coordination. Est. product + legal loop.

Customer quotes (annotated):
- "We lost 2 hours investigating a model switch without any trace" — Beta, mid-market fintech (calls 2027-09-07).
- "The console shows 20% canary but we can’t tell which users hit it" — Delta, adtech (email thread).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much detail do we put in logs vs. privacy/sensitive prompts? Need redaction guidelines. (Action: sync with security).
- Cheap-variant toggle: do we expose only suggestions (opt-in) or enforce server-side? (Tradeoff: safety vs. friction).

Next steps (who does what):
- This week: eng-observability to sketch audit-log reason codes (owner: Liam). Due: 2027-09-24.
- Product-console to prototype deterministic rollout preview wireframe (owner: Riley). Due: 2027-09-28.
- CS to compile 6 customer reproducer payloads for sandboxing play (owner: Aisha). Due: 2027-09-22.

Quick wins backlog (prioritized):
- Add fallback reason code to audit logs (high)
- Deterministic rollout preview in console (high)
- Per-route cheap-variant toggle (medium)
- Documentation: "What to do when routing falls back" (low effort doc)

Risks / Notes to legal & security:
- Need to ensure logs avoid persisting raw prompt text for regulated customers. Add redaction + retention policy.
- Any server-side control that recommends cheaper models should emit explicit quality-regression telemetry.

Appendix: related tickets and snippets
- CS-4812 (customer incident log) — contains timeline for Alpha incident.
- PR#2896 (console) — small UI changes to rollout create flow; might be extended for preview.
- Slack thread: #customer-voices thread 8a9f2e for direct customer quotes and attachments.

Notes to self: keep this doc ephemeral — move to canonical Confluence once micro-patches land. Use the sandbox customers as early reviewers.
